data.title: QA Automation POC - Tool Selection, Evidence, Coverage and Pipeline Plan

body.value:
Decision requested: standardize Playwright for web regression, retain QA review of generated tests, and approve a staged CI pilot. Choose an AI authoring standard after a matched Codex/Claude benchmark rather than from unequal POCs.

Evidence snapshot: 8 October 2026. �Measured locally� means a saved execution artifact was inspected. �Reported� means a company document describes a run, without the original run artifacts available in this checkout. �Proposed� means not yet executed or deployed. Cases, executable tests, setup tests and assertions are counted separately.

Coverage correction: the available evidence does not substantiate �300 out of 400 completed.� The canonical RSA POC reports 449 catalogued cases, 61 implemented cases producing 71 tests, and 57 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed. It describes 388 cases as not started. Do not present those cases as impossible to automate.

1. QA automation tools and why Playwright

The browser framework executes and reports tests. Codex and Claude Code help author, investigate and maintain them. These are separate decisions. The alternatives below are a documented capability comparison; only Playwright was exercised in this POC. No comparative speed or cost benchmark was performed.

Tool

Strength and fit

Weakness / boundary

POC evidence and recommendation

Playwright

Browser actions with actionability checks; multiple pages; API requests; integrated HTML/JUnit reporting and traces. Good fit for RSA MVC/jQuery and Benefit Blazor.

Still requires reviewed assertions, stable selectors, valid accounts/data and lifecycle control. Browser emulation does not prove native-device or physical-service behavior.

RSA job detail opens in a new tab; cascading client/program/tier/privilege selects are exercised. Benefit Save/detail/CMS rendering passes. Recommended web runtime.

Selenium WebDriver

Standards-based browser automation and broad language/browser ecosystem; useful where a mature WebDriver suite already exists.

Our project would still need to assemble a runner, assertions and equivalent evidence/reporting conventions. Switching adds migration work; no local comparative reliability result exists.

Not evaluated experimentally in this POC. Keep existing Selenium assets if valuable; no evidence supports a blanket migration claim.

Cypress

Interactive developer workflow, browser testing and retry behavior. Viable for suitable frontend-focused flows.

Its architecture has trade-offs; multi-tab testing can use the official Puppeteer plugin. That adds a different approach for RSA new-tab flows.

Not evaluated experimentally. Prefer Playwright for the already-proven RSA page/popup workflow, not because Cypress is categorically incapable.

Appium

Native/hybrid mobile automation and device interactions; complements browser testing for Aspire Partner.

Device/emulator setup and driver maintenance; browser success does not prove GPS, camera, notifications or real field operations.

Recommended for native-device scenarios as a separate workstream, not as the browser-suite replacement.

The selection is grounded in existing executable tests and evidence, not popularity. RSA TC05.2 follows a real new tab; TC05.3 creates a job through dependent selects and reads the assigned job ID. Benefit TC-VENDOR-CREATE-002 checks Save success, navigation and 19 CMS-to-rendering comparisons. Screenshot/video/trace artifacts and JUnit summaries are produced by the same test command.

Official capability references: Playwright actionability, trace viewer, Selenium WebDriver, Cypress trade-offs, Appium scope.

Corrections to older wording: Selenium supports explicit waits, so sleeps are not an unavoidable Selenium requirement. Cypress now documents a multi-tab plugin; avoid �cannot drive a second tab at all.� Paid cloud orchestration is different from whether CI jobs can be distributed. Playwright has no framework licence fee, but engineering, maintenance, AI seats and CI compute still cost money.

2. Codex versus Claude Code: observed results

Evidence

Claude Code POC

Codex POC

Interpretation

Author attribution

The canonical company page explicitly says Claude Code built the earlier RSA suite.

The Benefit creation and rendering work was performed in this Codex session.

Attribution is supported for these two workloads; the workshop RSA smoke suite is not independently agent-attributed.

Scope and output

Reported: 449-case catalogue, 61 implemented cases, 71 parameterized tests; auth, job-list and a small cross-cutting subset.

Measured: Benefit vendor creation, successful DB read and creation, and a separate Save/detail/rendering TC with 19 comparisons.

Different scope, apps and acceptance criteria; counts do not establish an AI winner.

Executed results

Reported: 57 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed in 8.6 minutes on 4 workers. Known defects use expected-failure annotations.

Measured latest UI run: 1 functional TC plus 1 login setup passed, 0 failed/skipped; 19 rendering comparisons passed. Suite 286.861 seconds; functional TC 171.956 seconds.

Case runtime measures test execution, not authoring speed. A green run with skips or expected failures is not complete defect-free coverage.

Problem-solving evidence

Reported: source review corrected NEW badge expectations and identified prefix/name-search rules and security findings.

Measured: user correction identified the global Thailand prerequisite; reload enabled required inputs. AWS credentials were passed in memory.

Both show value from repo/context access and iteration. Human review and corrections were necessary.

Limits observed

9 tests lacked accounts, 2 needed Okta identity, 1 needed a signed auth hash, 2 needed seed data.

Initial false blocker classification, incomplete dependent rows, input-loop errors and comparison-format assumptions required correction. AWS session expiry blocked final DB/CMS replay.

Neither agent should be treated as an autonomous oracle. Classify app defects separately from test defects and environment blockers.

Full DB/CMS consistency

No matching vendor-creation benchmark from Claude was found.

Vendor 20414 was created and core shared fields matched. Full replay is pending: initial availability and asset checks were test errors, corrected but not successfully rerun after AWS expiry.

Do not label TC-VENDOR-CREATE-001 fully passed. Latest TC002 tests UI/CMS rendering and does not replace database consistency verification.

Recommendation: standardize the generated test format, review criteria and Playwright runtime now. Continue the pilot with the agents already in use. There is insufficient matched evidence to claim Codex or Claude Code is universally better, cheaper or faster. Existing RSA authorship favors continuity with its current tool; the measured Benefit run demonstrates Codex viability.

Proposed matched benchmark: give both agents the same five reviewed cases (RSA dependent job creation, popup detail, API failure fallback, Benefit vendor Save/detail/CMS, and a read-only DB consistency check), same repo commit, UAT fixtures, permissions, browser/runtime, access and time allowance. Record agent/model version, prompts, first-run success, time to an accepted test, human interventions, corrections, false defect reports, seeded-fault detection, maintenance after a controlled UI change and actual billed usage. Execute identical acceptance checks and compare at least three recorded authoring runs plus repeated regression runs. Pre-agree scoring with QA; do not substitute code-line or test-count totals for correctness.

3. Strengths, weaknesses and recommendation with proof

Finding

Evidence

Decision

Playwright produces inspectable results

RSA local JUnit/JSON reports and stored trace/video/screenshots; Benefit pass report with Save/detail screenshots and per-field CMS comparison.

Use the standard Playwright report and retained CI artifacts as the proof of execution.

Integration consistency can be automated

Vendor 20414 returned a CMSId and exactly one BenefitDB row; name, address, phone, status, country, category/module, client/program and contacts matched the submitted values in the initial comparison.

Use browser + API + SELECT checks together. DB access is a prerequisite, not an inherent automation limitation.

A passing browser test can expose only part of an integration

TC002 checks published CMS against rendered values. It does not prove rollback, RSA dispatch, real SMS delivery or every native-device path.

Declare boundaries per TC and add integration/device tests where necessary.

Generated tests can be wrong

Global market and reload were missed initially; comparison used wrong Codename casing and assumed asset ID equals delivery URL storage GUID. Those assumptions were corrected.

Require peer review and deliberately seeded faults before promotion to a release gate.

Not every populated field reached the request

The saved vendor 20414 payload contained an empty mailing-details object and several empty optional restaurant collections despite earlier input attempts. Stored blank values matching a blank request is not proof of intended input coverage.

Add UI-to-payload retention assertions for optional fields and investigate binding or test interaction before claiming all-elements coverage.

Negative detection is valuable but evidence strength differs

Workshop README reports a 13-green -> 2-red/11-green -> revert -> 13-green rehearsal on 2 October; latest local saved run is only 6 green tests. Original red-run artifacts were not available.

Retain before/fault/after run IDs and reports in CI. Treat the rehearsal as documented, not independently reproduced here.

4. Completed automation and the remaining scope

Inventory / run

Verified count

Meaning and limitation

Canonical RSA catalogue

449 cases / 22 sheets; priorities P1 234, P2 181, P3 34

Reported by the canonical company POC page, retrieved 8 October. The workbook and original larger suite are absent from this checkout.

Canonical implemented scope

61 unique cases -> 71 tests; 10 files

Reported. 61/449 = 13.6% implemented case coverage. Parameterization increases test count; it does not create extra business cases.

Canonical last full run

57 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed; 8.6 minutes / 4 workers

Reported execution. 57/71 = 80.3% test pass share; 14/71 = 19.7% skipped. This is not 80.3% product coverage.

Canonical remaining work

388 cases not started

Reported. No evidence classifies all 388 as non-automatable.

Workshop RSA runnable inventory

13 tests in 6 files: 12 functional checks plus 1 authentication setup

Measured locally with Playwright --list. Login, dealer, provider, draft announcements and jobs.

Workshop latest saved run

6 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped; 38.882 seconds

Measured JSON/JUnit: 5 dealer/job functional checks plus authentication setup on 7 October. Do not claim all 13 ran in this saved execution.

Benefit latest saved UI run

2 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped; 286.861 seconds

Measured: TC-VENDOR-CREATE-002 and login setup on 8 October. Vendor 20415; 19 CMS-to-rendering checks passed.

Boss figure: 300 / 400

Not verified

If this refers to a newer pack, reconcile its version and case IDs first. Numerically 75%, but neither implementation nor execution of those 300 is established by this evidence.

The 14 reported RSA skips have specific enabling conditions. They should not be labelled 14 scenarios that cannot be automated.

Reported blocking category

Tests

What is automatable / enabling action

Missing role, agent, inactive and impersonation accounts

9

Provide least-privilege UAT accounts, then run role-specific assertions. Missing credentials are an environment blocker.

Okta test identity / interactive sign-in

2

Application behavior after an approved test identity/session can be tested; real interactive MFA may require a human or an approved test authentication design. Do not bypass MFA to make CI green.

Server-minted signed authentication hash

1

Use a controlled fixture/minting mechanism that reproduces the signed path. Hard-coding a guessed hash does not test the real flow.

Job reference / assigned-truck fixture missing

2

Prepare reproducible seeded jobs or approved UAT fixture IDs with those relationships. Then the UI assertions are automatable.

For any newer 400-case pack, assign every case one of the classifications below. Each row needs Case ID, feature, priority, intended outcome, current implementation and run status, automatic portion, manual portion, blocker, owner, enabling action and evidence link. Counts must sum to the reviewed inventory. The examples are proposed classification guidance, not a claim that these exact cases account for the alleged remaining 100.

Classification

Representative scenario

Automatic portion

Why not full today / enabling action

Full automation candidate

Login, validation, search/filter, dependent dropdowns, create/read-back, status rules, role checks

Deterministic browser/API assertions with reviewed expected behavior

Implement reviewed cases and isolate test data. These are demonstrated by the existing web POCs.

Full automation with access/data prerequisites

BenefitDB/CMS/RSA field consistency, assigned provider/truck, signed auth path

UI + API + SELECT + correlation IDs and bounded polling

Missing account, DB access, fixture, signed token or network route. This is blocked automation, not inherently manual.

Partial end-to-end automation

SMS/email notifications and third-party provider callback flows

Verify request, accepted response, event and test inbox/callback where a controlled integration exists

Real handset receipt, external vendor behavior or human response is not proved by a mocked response. Add test-device/test-provider evidence where feasible.

Partial operational automation

Dispatch and roadside assistance completion

Create/assign jobs, check transitions, provider-app events, timestamps and attachments

Actual travel, towing quality, safe service and customer experience need operational observation. A digital status is not proof the physical service happened.

Device automation plus human field checks

GPS tracking, camera capture, background notifications, unstable connectivity

Appium/device harness, location injection, network shaping, push/photo checks on controlled devices

Browser emulation cannot validate native OS behavior or real-road GPS quality. Add the device suite; retain field acceptance checks.

Partial visual/exploratory automation

Layout checks, accessibility checks, new workflows and subjective usability

Screenshot diffs and machine-checkable accessibility/structure rules

Human judgement determines whether wording, usability and service experience meet business needs. Baselines need review.

Manual acceptance portion

Real MFA approval, CAPTCHA completion as an anti-bot control, physical service quality

Surrounding app states and error handling can be checked automatically with approved fixtures

The human or physical action remains manual under the actual production-like process. Separate that portion instead of marking the whole case impossible.

Not started / not yet assessed

Any unreviewed feature sheet

Unknown until requirements and fixture needs are reviewed

No implementation is not proof of a technical limitation. Assign an owner and assess before forecasting coverage.

A useful 300/400 statement must say whether 300 means reviewed cases, implemented cases, latest passed cases or cases suitable for automation. Report three measures separately: implemented case coverage, executed case coverage, and latest pass rate. Also report partial cases, blocked cases, manual acceptance portions and unassessed cases. Do not sum assertions, setup tests or repeated runs into case coverage.

5. Pipeline integration plan and POC evidence

Current status: local runs, HTML/JUnit outputs, retained evidence, a proposed CodeBuild buildspec and a locally checked report gate. No new CodeBuild project, pipeline stage, scheduled run or release gate has been created in this task. Existing application deployment pipelines are not evidence that QA automation is integrated.

Milestone

Work

Evidence required before claiming completion

A. Freeze the reviewed smoke pack

Reconcile workbook/version and case IDs; restore the canonical larger suite if it is to be used; define read-only smoke and controlled write packs.

Reviewed inventory, source commit, test --list output and pack manifest. For the workshop pack, the measured list is 13 tests including setup.

B. Establish unattended prerequisites

Run a dedicated Linux CodeBuild test project with a compatible Node/browser image, injected QA credentials and suitable network access. SQL checks use a VPC route rather than a developer desktop tunnel.

Preflight run proves environment, IAM read permissions, account roles, DB schema, DNS/TLS and fixture readiness. No interactive aws login in CI.

C. Demonstrate one CI run

Use npm ci, install browsers/dependencies, run the smoke pack serially, and publish JUnit plus restricted HTML/trace/video artifacts on success and failure.

CodeBuild run ID, source SHA, timestamps, artifact/report links, counts and per-TC results. This has not yet been measured.

D. Demonstrate fault detection

In an isolated fixture, introduce a reviewed data/API failure, execute, then revert and rerun.

Before/fault/after reports show the intended TC fails and recovers; retain fixture cleanup evidence. Do not disrupt shared UAT clients.

E. Stabilize before gating releases

QA owns triage; distinguish app defect, test defect, environment block and expected failure. Proposed target: 10 consecutive unattended smoke runs without unexplained skips/flakes.

Recorded stability history and triage ownership; proposed target is not an achieved KPI.

F. Integrate triggers and expand

Post-SIT-deploy smoke, nightly regression/integration pack, controlled UAT release-candidate pack. Add native mobile/Appium and contract tests separately.

Actual trigger configuration and run links. P1 failures/missing mandatory cases block promotion under an agreed policy; expected known defects stay visible.

Proposed execution sequence: deploy SIT/UAT build -> target/credential/fixture preflight -> reviewed smoke pack -> API/DB/CMS checks where applicable -> result classification -> publish evidence -> quality gate -> release decision. Start with one worker; parallelize only after each test owns independent data. Automatic retry of create flows is disabled in the draft because it can duplicate records until idempotency and cleanup are implemented.

The attached buildspec.poc.yml targets the standalone ai-workshop repository, with roadside-web/ at its root. CodeBuild project credentials and browser-capable Linux image must be configured first. The app deployment may remain Windows-based; the QA runner is a separate project. Role/secret/VPC/schedule changes and deployment were not performed.

The local report gate was checked with five policy fixtures: accept a clean run; reject failure, skip, empty run and incomplete pack. It parsed the saved RSA report (6 tests, all green) and correctly rejected it when the required full workshop pack was set to 13. It accepted the saved Benefit report when its expected size was 2. This proves local result consumption and pack completeness policy, not cloud execution.

CodeBuild officially supports JUnit reports. Its buildspec defines report groups/artifacts and supports secret references; VPC-enabled builds can reach private resources with the required network configuration. See CodeBuild test reports, buildspec reference and VPC support. Playwright documents browser installation and CI execution in its CI guide.

Keep credentials and auth state out of source and shared reports. Restrict trace/video artifacts because they can capture tokens and customer data. Publish approved synthetic screenshots and summaries to this page. Use a reviewed cleanup process for created vendors, jobs, drafts and staged CMS assets. A passing test without cleanup is not pipeline readiness.

Primary internal source: Web Automation testing by Playwright and AI. Its older framework claims and cost extrapolations are not reproduced as measured facts here. The hypothetical 8-minute manual case, release frequency, annual QA-day savings and AI seat costs require current team data and procurement verification before budgeting.

Open evidence requests: the specific 400-case workbook/version and corresponding 300 implemented/pass case IDs; full source and run artifacts for the reported larger RSA suite; a matched agent benchmark; and a real CI run with artifact links. Until supplied, the recommendation above is a justified POC decision with explicit limits, not a certified 75% coverage claim.
